surprises.description: The preview used the Q3 adjusted EBITDA guide of $3.4–$3.6 million as the benchmark. AEYE reported a record $3.9 million, with a 35% margin, a substantial beat against that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 58% year-over-year to a record $3.9 million, lifting adjusted EBITDA margin to 35% from 24% a year earlier.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case was that full-year EBITDA guidance would be reaffirmed, while a raise to at least $13.0 million was the bull trigger and the exit run rate was expected to exceed $15 million. AEYE raised its full-year target to $13.4–$13.6 million and lifted the Q4 annualized run-rate target to above $17 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $13.4-$13.6 million (~50% growth) and now targets a Q4 annualized run rate exceeding $17 million, up from a prior $15 million expectation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … FY reaffirmed; $15M exit run-rate confirmed”; “A third consecutive EBITDA raise (≥$13.0M) is the bull trigger”; “Exit run-rate Adj. EBITDA > $15M annualized by YE26.”

surprises.description: The preview described the GAAP-to-adjusted earnings gap as a source of likely headline noise, but AEYE reported positive GAAP net income rather than a loss. The company moved from a $0.6 million loss to $1 million of income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 GAAP net income turned positive at $1 million ($0.08 per share), reversing a $0.6 million net loss ($0.04 per share loss) in the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect the same mechanical noise tonight”; the preview also flags “the GAAP crossover” as an issue to watch.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted margin quality and cautioned that EBITDA upside from cost cuts should be discounted, but AEYE reported a sharp improvement in gross margin tied to lower cost of revenue and AI efficiencies. This points to an efficiency-driven source of improvement beyond the preview’s stated concern about operating-expense cuts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded over 550 basis points year-over-year to 88%, as cost of revenue declined 19% from AI-driven efficiencies even as revenue rose.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin 84% (79% GAAP)”; “If EBITDA upside comes from opex cuts rather than revenue, the market should discount it.”

surprises.description: The preview expected partner/marketplace growth around 16% year over year. The reported 14% growth was still positive but came in below that stated benchmark.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “59% of ARR, +16% YoY, driven by SMB marketplace and state/local government.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated roughly 129,000 customers and cited an increase of 9,000 year over year. AEYE reported about 130,000 customers, but growth of 6% year over year, indicating slower customer-count growth than the preview’s benchmark suggested.

The preview expected litigation expense to decline in the second half but did not quantify the reduction. AEYE said it had already fallen about 50% sequentially in Q3 and would decline further in Q4, providing a stronger quantified cost tailwind than the preview specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Litigation expense fell approximately 50% sequentially in Q3 and is expected to decline further in Q4, supporting substantial cash generation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided litigation expense down in H2'26.”

surprises.description: The preview mentioned supplemental AI products as a possible ARPU lever but did not identify upcoming launches or their stated capability. AEYE announced two October AI products, Agentic Audits and SDK MCP, that it said can detect up to 50% more high-severity issues than automation alone; the call did not quantify resulting revenue or ARPU.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched two new AI products (Agentic Audits and SDK MCP) in October that can detect up to 50% more high-severity issues than automation alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has flagged ‘supplemental AI products’ as the ARPU lever.”
